item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Portrait From a Seventies Film

turns.text: Make this look like a still from a 1970s movie—warm faded colours and film grain. Keep her recognisable and keep the square framing. No text.

item.tests: Applies a convincing 1970s film treatment while preserving the uploaded portrait's identity and composition.

answer_sheet.Style and mood: A nostalgic 1970s colour film still, with warm faded colours and visible film grain.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: Her identity, curly dark hair, sweater, pose and park setting.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One square image; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The woman remains recognisable as the woman in the source portrait.
Her curly dark hair, sweater and head-and-shoulders framing are retained.
The park background remains identifiable rather than becoming a different setting.
Warm, faded colour grading and visible film grain give the image a 1970s film-still appearance.
The output is square and contains no added text.

turns.text: Make this pic look like a still from a 1970s movie—warm faded colours and film grain. Keep her recognisable and keep the square framing. No text. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
The cheapest listed option for this edit is **Flux 2 Klein on the free plan, with one image at 640px: from 5 credits**. I can’t verify your balance or a firm final charge with the tools available, so I haven’t started anything or spent credits.

I’d keep:
- Her recognisable facial features and the square composition
- Warm, faded 1970s colour grading with subtle film grain
- No text

**Cheaper or smaller?** 640px is the smallest supported output setting; there’s no lower-priced size listed. “Shorter” doesn’t apply to a still image. For **zero Magic Hour credits**, a photo editor’s warmth, fade and grain adjustments could achieve this look without generative editing—and better preserve her face exactly.

Would you prefer the zero-credit editing instructions, or proceed with the lowest-priced AI option, listed from 5 credits?

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the edit because your account has **insufficient credits**. No image was generated and no credits were spent.

You can still get this look for free in a photo editor: increase warmth slightly, reduce saturation and contrast, lift the blacks for a faded finish, and add fine film grain. Keep the square crop unchanged to preserve the framing and her appearance.
